def is_safe_name(name: str) -> bool:
    """True when name is a plain relative path that stays inside the notes directory:
    non-empty, not absolute, no ".." component, no backslash, no NUL, no drive prefix."""
    ex is_safe_name("a.txt") == True
    ex is_safe_name("sub/a.txt") == True
    ex is_safe_name("") == False
    ex is_safe_name("../secret.txt") == False
    ex is_safe_name("a/../../b") == False
    ex is_safe_name("/etc/passwd") == False
    ex is_safe_name("a\\b") == False
    if "\\" in name or "\0" in name or ":" in name:
        return False
    for part in name.split("/"):
        if part == "" or part == "..":
            return False
    return True

def first_readable(names: list[str]) -> str uses fs:
    """Text of the first name in names that can be read as a file inside the directory notes, or "" if none can.
    Reads happen only within fs confined to notes (with fs = fs.sub("notes")). Names are untrusted: a name that
    fails is_safe_name, is missing, or is unreadable is skipped."""
    with fs = fs.sub("notes"):
        for name in names:
            if not is_safe_name(name):
                continue
            text: str | None = fs.read(name) else None
            if text is not None:
                return text
    return ""
